results.title: S. Korea needs closer security partners in uncertain times
results.content: As President Lee Jae Myung was discussing geopolitical disruption at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines on Nov. 17, Russian military aircraft flew into South Korea’s air defense identification zone. Japan was targeted on the same day: two suspected Russian aircraft entered its airspace off the archipelago's southwestern coast. This incident marked an escalation in hostile activity against Japan over the last two months, after Russia arrested a Japanese journalist and expanded the list of Japan Tobacco International businesses placed under temporary administration. Both South Korea and Japan scrambled jets in response to Russia’s incursions, and the incidents were a timely reminder that threats to Seoul and Tokyo’s security are ever present. results.title: Seoul shares open higher amid lingering AI woes
results.content: Korean shares opened higher Thursday after the previous session's sharp decline, as investors remained concerned about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. After opening 1.01 percent higher, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) increased 62.07 points, or 1.32 percent, to 4,759.58 as of 9:15 a.m. On Wednesday, the KOSPI plunged more than 6 percent, reversing the previous session's rally, as an overnight sell-off in technology stocks on Wall Street revived concerns over the sustainability of the AI trade. Beyond AI-related concerns, investors are also assessing U.S. plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from 14 countries, including South Korea. results.title: Russia plays dangerous airspace game
results.content: Residents of Ulleung Island in the East Sea were thrown into a panic on Tuesday morning when an emergency shelter alert was suddenly issued. They were initially told that North Korean aircraft were on the verge of entering South Korea’s sovereign airspace over the island. Minutes later, the evacuation alert was lifted, allowing residents to breathe a sigh of relief. It turned out that two Russian bombers, escorted by two fighter jets, had entered the Korea Air Defense Identification Zone (KADIZ) near the island. KADIZ is an airspace zone extending beyond South Korea’s territorial airspace, in which aircraft are expected to identify themselves and report their positions. As they continued to approach the airspace boundary, the Republic of Korea Air Force scrambled fighter jets to visually identify the Russian aircraft and warn them against entering the country's sovereign space. results.title: Korea knocked out of Davis Cup after narrow loss to Italy
results.content: Korea has been eliminated from the Davis Cup after a narrow loss to the three-time defending champion Italy in the quarterfinals of the top men's tennis team competition in Italy on Wednesday (local time). The underdog Korea stole one singles match but ultimately lost 2-1 in the best-of-three battle on the indoor hard court set up at BolognaFiere in Bologna, as the home team moved a step closer to its fourth consecutive title. After the two countries split the two singles matches, Italy's Andrea Vavassori and Matteo Berrettini needed tiebreakers in both sets to hold off Kwon Soon-woo and Chung Hyeon 7-6 (7-2), 7-6 (13-11) in the deciding doubles match. In its Davis Cup quarterfinals debut, Korea was the lowest seed in the tournament, with no player inside the top 100 in the singles or doubles rankings. results.title: US proposes excess capacity tariffs on Korean goods within agreed 15% ceiling
results.content: WASHINGTON — The United States proposed Wednesday imposing tariffs of up to 15 percent on Korean goods over alleged excess manufacturing capacity, taking into account a bilateral trade agreement and existing tariffs. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) announced the proposed measures as it determined that the acts, policies and practices of Korea and 13 other economies, including China, Japan and the European Union (EU), relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors were unreasonable and burdened or restricted U.S. commerce. The USTR proposed applying tariffs of up to 15 percent on all Korean goods, net of most-favored-nation (MFN) tariff rates and existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods. results.title: NK leader stresses use of tactical nukes in diverse areas
results.content: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un has visited nuclear material production facilities and a research institute and called for using tactical nuclear weapons across a wide range of missions, state media reported Thursday. Kim visited the sites the previous day to review progress on the nuclear strategy set out at a key party congress earlier this year, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported. It did not disclose where the facilities are located. During his inspection, Kim said North Korea is "systematically and steadily expanding nuclear-material production capacity" to strengthen and advance the country's nuclear arsenal. He stressed the need to use tactical nuclear weapons in "diverse areas for various missions." results.title: AI music tops local chart: What you need to know
results.content: A song written with assistance from artificial intelligence (AI) has topped Korea's most closely watched music chart for the first time, raising questions about how the country's music industry should handle songs created with AI. MEOMURU's rock ballad "The Adult I Dreamed Of" reached No. 1 on Melon's Top 100 on Nov. 13, months after Joseon HipHop's AI-assisted "Forest of the Heart" peaked at No. 89 on the chart. Released June 23, the ballad gained traction through Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts before topping YouTube's daily popular music video chart in Korea in September. With no established fandom or television promotion behind it, the song won over listeners in their 30s and 40s in particular with lyrics reflecting on the gap between childhood aspirations and adult reality. results.title: Blue Elephant bets on landmark stores to build global eyewear brand
results.content: Blue Elephant is accelerating its global expansion, starting with the United States and Japan, by opening brand-inspired stores in strategic locations to raise its profile among local consumers. The budget eyewear company, drawing on its experience operating 32 directly managed stores in Korea since 2019, including in tourist hotspots such as Seongsu, Myeong-dong and Jeju Island, has opened outlets in California and Tokyo. Fueled by a growing number of foreign customers, the Seoul-based company is seeing international consumers account for an increasing share of its sales both at home and abroad. In August, Blue Elephant opened its first U.S. flagship store in Beverly Hills, within the Golden Triangle, a local retail district home to global luxury fashion and beauty brands as well as restaurants. results.title: Korean War veteran still carries bullet near his heart 73 years after battle
results.content: PYEONGTAEK, Gyeonggi Province — On July 20, 1953, just a week before the Korean War armistice was signed, Ryu Jae-sik and a Chinese soldier stood with their guns pointed at each other. Both fired. The Chinese soldier’s bullet struck Ryu’s shoulder, broke eight of his ribs and lodged near his heart. It is still there, 73 years later. Ryu, who now heads the Seoul branch of the Korean War Veterans Association, recalled his days on the battlefield during a visit to the U.S. Eighth Army headquarters at Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, Nov. 5. A native of Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, Ryu was an 18-year-old student when the war broke out in 1950. He and his friends hid in the mountains to avoid being conscripted by North Korean forces, catching frogs and grasshoppers to eat when they ran out of food. results.title: Tunisia Embassy celebrates 2026 World Olive Tree Day in Seoul
results.content: Since ancient times, the olive tree has served as a symbol of peace, wisdom and harmony. To honor the 3,000-year heritage of the olive tree and its cultural, environmental and economic significance across the Mediterranean region, the Embassy of Tunisia in Korea hosted an event marking the upcoming World Olive Tree Day at the ambassador’s residence in northeastern Seoul’s Seongbuk District, Friday. UNESCO officially established the annual observance on Nov. 26 during the 40th session of its General Conference in 2019, following an initiative by Tunisia and Lebanon. This year's event, A Taste of Tunisia, was aimed at bringing together Korean importers, distributors, food industry professionals and media, combining a celebration of Tunisia's olive-growing heritage with an opportunity to explore new commercial partnerships in Korea's fast-growing market. results.title: Building a community for Black creatives in Seoul
results.content: When Marie Noel moved to Korea in 2024, the plan was simple: find a way to continue her filmmaking career as a writer and actor. Her profession had given her opportunities to travel across Austria, Germany and the U.K. In all these places she went, she found herself in spaces where representation and access were not always guaranteed. As soon as she began reconnecting with filmmaking in Korea, she was confronted with a similar reality about visibility and representation. Identifying and connecting Black creatives specifically required time and deliberate effort. The reality was further compounded by the fact that Black creatives were living and working across Korea and pursuing their own artistic interests, yet many were doing so independently, oblivious of each other, in the same industry. results.title: N. Korea expels Swiss diplomat over sanctions weeks after office reopening
results.content: North Korea has expelled the head of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang and ordered the envoy to leave within 48 hours, its foreign ministry said on Wednesday, in a spat over sanctions less than a month after Bern reopened the office. The ministry said the move was in response to the Swiss decision to put sanctions on North Korea's Songdowon International Children's Camp, calling it an overtly hostile act in a statement carried by the state-run Korean Central News Agency. Pyongyang's Foreign Ministry summoned the head of the diplomatic office, Sylvain Astier, and handed him a memorandum urging him to close the office, the news agency said. "The Foreign Ministry of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea declared the head of the Swiss Diplomatic Office in the DPRK persona non grata and urged him to leave the country within 48 hours," it said, using the country's official name.

results.title: 'Hope' wins top Blue Dragon award; Sul, Jeon take acting honors for 'Possible Love'
results.content: Director Na Hong-jin's sci-fi thriller "Hope" won best picture at the 47th Blue Dragon Film Awards on Wednesday, while Lee Chang-dong's "Possible Love" emerged as the night's biggest winner with four awards, including both top acting honors. "Hope," which competed at this year's Cannes Film Festival, entered the ceremony at KBS Hall in Seoul with a leading 10 nominations and also won the cinematography and lighting award. Accepting the best picture trophy, Na drew laughter from the audience by joking that he should have won the award at Cannes. "They should have given me this at Cannes. Why here instead?" he said. Na then credited the cast and crew, describing the experience of making the film as one of the happiest and most memorable times of his life. results.title: US proposes tariffs over excess production, retains 15% cap for Korea, Japan, EU
results.content: WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in U.S. midterm elections. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20 percent to 40 percent to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting. But the U.S. Trade Representative's office said it intends to cap new tariffs at lower levels agreed under trade deals that are completed or still under negotiation. In unveiling the results of an eight-month unfair trade practices investigation into excess industrial capacity, USTR aims to more fully rebuild Trump's tariff leverage after the Supreme Court in February struck down his broad global duties under a national emergencies law. results.title: Mathmatician-turned-Buddhist monk leans into inner cultivation for AI era
results.content: “Inner cultivation to manage alienation and depression will become increasingly important in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). We need ‘metacognition’ — the ability to objectively observe our own mental state — to regulate and overcome our emotions.” Ven. Ilmuk, a 61-year-old Buddhist monk who has practiced meditation in Korea and abroad for 30 years and taught meditation, has published his first book in five years, "Buddha’s Breathing Meditation" (Bulkwang Publishing). Based on the early Buddhist scripture "Anapanasati Sutta" (Mindfulness of Breathing), the book offers a detailed guide to the principles and practice of breathing meditation. It covers everything from the basic steps of observing one’s breath to obstacles that hinder meditation and ways to overcome them, as well as the process of cultivating concentration and wisdom to end suffering.
